title: A within-day DM and peak-frequency relation in FRB 20220912A weakens after burst-shape controls in CHIME Catalog 2
abstract: We test fitted dispersion measure (DM) against peak frequency within each source and day in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. Two repeaters pass fixed sample-size cuts. For FRB 20220912A, 272 bursts on 84 days give a slope of 0.869 pc cm^-3 per 100 MHz, with a nominal 95% day-bootstrap interval of 0.429 to 1.342. Early and late slopes are positive. A joint fit with time, bandwidth, width, S/N and flagged channel fraction gives 0.349, with an interval of -0.048 to 0.771. FRB 20180916B has no stable full-sample association. A simple emission-delay model with cubic frequency dependence does not improve later prediction. Same-fit parameter errors and burst structure remain possible explanations. No independent telescope confirms this relation. We report a catalog audit, not a new physical DM change or object. Code, frozen events, source hashes, all tests and offline instructions are included.
